title: The Half Proof
prompt:
**Scenario.** A greedy passes every random test up to n = 1000 that you generate. What is the correct next step before trusting it in a contest?

**Which approach is the best fit? The program only needs to print the letter.**

**A)** Submit it — random coverage at n = 1000 is strong evidence

**B)** Write the one-sentence exchange/induction proof; if it fails on equal keys or dependencies, construct targeted adversarial cases

**C)** Increase n to 10^5 and rerun random tests

**D)** Trust it but implement the DP fallback anyway

tests.name: answer
tests.hint: Random tests rarely hit the structures that break greedies (equal keys, dependency corners). Proof first; the failure modes of the proof tell you exactly which adversarial inputs to build.
